meta.title: wickwatch – self-hosted dashboard for cTrader trading bots
meta.description: Monitor and control your cTrader bots (cBots) in Docker: instances, positions, deals and prop-firm challenge limits in one self-hosted dashboard. Open source under AGPL-3.0.
nav.label: Sections
hero.title: Keep watch over your trading bots
hero.lead: wickwatch is a self-hosted dashboard for trading bots, starting with cTrader cBots in Docker: see what runs where and with which parameters, start and stop instances, follow positions and deals live, and keep prop-firm challenge limits in view.
hero.alt: wickwatch overview: three accounts with balance, equity and today's P&L, an alert for a bot that failed to log in, and the table of bot instances with status, uptime and last log line.
features.title: Your trading bots on one screen
features.intro: wickwatch watches and controls; your strategies stay your own. It does not trade by itself, and it makes no promises about profits.
features.overview.title: Overview
features.overview.text: Accounts with balance, equity, today's P&L, open positions and pending orders. All instances with status, uptime and their last log line. Alerts for stopped, crashed or disconnected bots, broker errors and challenge limits.
features.instances.title: Instances
features.instances.text: Start, stop, restart. Create bots from an uploaded algo with a form built from its parameters; load or download parameter files. Every save is a version you can restore, and parameter templates switch any instance of the algo to a saved set.
features.log.title: Live log
features.log.text: Follow each bot's log live, search it in a larger view, and download the last 24 hours, 7 days or everything as a text file.
features.stop.title: Emergency stop
features.stop.text: One button per account stops its bots, cancels its orders and closes its positions. Always with confirmation, always in the audit log.
features.challenges.title: Prop challenges
features.challenges.text: Profit target, daily loss, drawdown, trading days and duration per account, with templates for FTMO and The Trading Pit. A warning before the firm closes an account that has not traded for too long. An optional loss guard runs the emergency stop before a limit is used up.
features.security.title: Secure by default
features.security.text: Built-in login with optional two-factor authentication and read-only users. Broker credentials encrypted at rest. Docker only through a socket proxy.
features.api.title: API and AI assistants
features.api.text: A REST API with OpenAPI docs and API tokens for your scripts. AI assistants that speak the Model Context Protocol (MCP) read accounts, challenge limits, instances, logs and alerts, so you can ask them whether your bots are running. Read-only: they never start, stop or trade.
showcase.instance.title: Every instance in detail
showcase.instance.text: Key figures, the realised P&L curve and the live log side by side; below them open positions, pending orders and the trade history with risk in % and R per trade.
showcase.instance.item1: Key figures for 7, 30 or 90 days: trades, win rate, profit factor, average win and loss, net result and R
showcase.instance.item2: Log filters for warnings and errors, or for the setups your bot logs as WW-SETUP lines
showcase.instance.item3: A details panel for every position, order and trade; the arrow keys step to the next one
showcase.instance.item4: A configuration tab with the parameters and every saved version, ready to restore
showcase.instance.alt: Instance page of the bot alpha-ger40-a: key figures for 30 days such as 39 trades, 64 % win rate and a net result of +2,576.25, the realised P&L curve and the live log.
showcase.account.title: Prop-firm challenge limits in view
showcase.account.text: The account page shows how far the profit target is and how much of the daily and total loss is used. Values that could not be measured exactly are marked as estimates.
showcase.account.item1: Daily loss with reset time and time zone, on balance or equity
showcase.account.item2: Max drawdown: static, trailing, or trailing on the end-of-day balance
showcase.account.alt: Account page of a demo prop challenge: balance and equity, the challenge with progress bars for profit target, daily loss, max drawdown, trading days and duration, and the account's instances.
showcase.phone.title: On your phone too
showcase.phone.text: The same dashboard, laid out for a small screen: alerts first, accounts as cards, actions below the headings with their labels. Dark and light mode, English and German, and a large touch target for the emergency stop.
showcase.phone.item1: Alerts to Telegram, Slack, Discord or ntfy when a bot stops, crashes or loses its connection, or a challenge limit gets close, and again when it is fine
showcase.phone.item2: A daily summary of your accounts at a time you choose
showcase.phone.item3: A heartbeat to a service like Healthchecks.io, which tells you when wickwatch itself is gone
showcase.phone.alt: wickwatch on a phone: an alert and the first account card with balance, equity, today's P&L and the emergency stop button.
how.title: Neutral core, pluggable adapters
how.intro: wickwatch knows neither your strategy nor your broker. Adapters connect it to where the bots run, to the broker and to the parameter format. The first ones run cTrader bots in Docker containers through the cTrader CLI; a demo adapter with fake data is built in.
how.runtime.title: Runtime: Docker
how.runtime.text: Finds labelled containers, starts and stops them, streams their logs. Docker is reached only through a docker-socket-proxy.
how.broker.title: Broker: cTrader CLI
how.broker.text: Accounts, balances, positions, orders, deals and algo metadata, one session per account.
how.config.title: Parameters: .cbotset
how.config.text: Reads and writes cTrader parameter files, so existing parameter sets keep working.
how.note: Another broker or platform? The adapter contracts are described in docs/ADAPTERS.md.
start.title: Try it with Docker in a minute
start.intro: The image starts with the demo adapter: fake accounts, instances, positions and logs, so you can look around without a broker or bots.
start.step1: Copy the setup token from the log line No admin yet. Open /setup and enter the setup token: …
start.step2: Open http://localhost:3000, enter the token, a user name and a password.
start.step3: Set up two-factor authentication now or later under Profile. The overview with demo data opens.
start.note: Running real bots on a server: the step-by-step install guide; all settings in the configuration reference. Put wickwatch behind your reverse proxy with HTTPS (nginx-proxy, Traefik or any other) and keep it out of public reach, e.g. with a VPN or an IP allowlist. wickwatch {{version}} is in early development and used on demo and prop-challenge accounts; what comes next is in the roadmap.
support.title: A hobby project, free and open
support.text: wickwatch is built in spare time and costs nothing. If it helps you, you can support it on Ko-fi or through GitHub Sponsors. Bug reports, ideas and pull requests help just as much.
footer.disclaimer: wickwatch is a monitoring and control tool, not financial advice. Trading involves risk; you are responsible for your bots and accounts. cTrader is a trademark of its respective owner; wickwatch is not affiliated with or endorsed by Spotware. wickwatch does not include any cTrader software; the cTrader CLI is subject to Spotware's licence terms.
footer.label: Links
footer.note: This site sets no cookies and uses no tracking. Fonts are served from this site.

topic.docker.metaTitle: Run cTrader cBots in Docker with a dashboard – wickwatch
topic.docker.metaDescription: Run cTrader bots (cBots) in Docker containers on a Linux server and manage them in one self-hosted dashboard: start, stop, parameters, logs, positions and an emergency stop.
topic.docker.title: Run cTrader cBots in Docker, with a dashboard
topic.docker.lead: The cTrader CLI runs a cBot without the desktop app, so a bot fits into a container on a Linux server. wickwatch adds what the command line leaves open: one place to see every bot with its account and its log, and to start, stop and reconfigure it.
topic.docker.s1.title: What wickwatch does with your bots
topic.docker.s1.1: Runs every instance as its own container, started through the cTrader CLI, and shows its status, uptime, broker connection and last log line.
topic.docker.s1.2: Creates a bot from an uploaded algo with a form built from the algo's parameters, or from an existing .cbotset file.
topic.docker.s1.3: Keeps every saved configuration as a version you can restore, and parameter templates that apply a named set of values to any instance of the algo.
topic.docker.s1.4: Follows positions, pending orders and deals per bot and per account, with realised P&L, win rate, profit factor and risk per trade.
topic.docker.s1.5: Starts bots again after a host or Docker restart if they were meant to run.
topic.docker.s1.6: Stops everything on an account with one emergency stop: bots stopped, orders cancelled, positions closed. Always with confirmation, always in the audit log.
topic.docker.s2.title: Two ways to define a bot
topic.docker.s2.text: Both can be mixed on one server.
topic.docker.s2.1: Set it up in wickwatch: upload the algo and create an instance. wickwatch creates, replaces and removes its container from the saved configuration.
topic.docker.s2.2: Define it yourself: wickwatch shows and controls every container from your own compose file that carries the label wickwatch.instance. It never replaces or removes such containers.
topic.docker.s3.title: What you need
topic.docker.s3.1: A Linux server with Docker and Compose. 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM are enough for the dashboard and a few bots.
topic.docker.s3.2: The cTrader CLI image, which you pull from Spotware yourself, and a cTrader ID with your accounts.
topic.docker.s3.3: Your compiled cBots as algo files.
topic.docker.s3.4: A reverse proxy with HTTPS in front of the dashboard, and a VPN or an IP allowlist: wickwatch can close positions and should stay out of public reach.
topic.docker.s4.title: Try it first, without a broker
topic.docker.s4.text: The image starts with a demo adapter: fake accounts, instances, positions and logs.
topic.docker.s4.next: For real bots, follow the step-by-step install guide; the compose files for nginx-proxy, Traefik or a port of its own are in the deployment examples. Docker is reached only through a docker-socket-proxy that allows the few API calls wickwatch needs.
topic.docker.note: cTrader is a trademark of its respective owner; wickwatch is not affiliated with or endorsed by Spotware and includes no cTrader software. The cTrader CLI is subject to Spotware's licence terms.
topic.prop.metaTitle: Prop-firm challenge limits for trading bots – wickwatch
topic.prop.metaDescription: Keep the daily loss, max drawdown and profit target of an FTMO or other prop-firm challenge in view while your bots trade, with alerts and an optional loss guard. Self-hosted, open source.
topic.prop.title: Keep prop-firm challenge limits in view while your bots trade
topic.prop.lead: A challenge ends at the daily loss or the maximum drawdown, whether you were watching or not. wickwatch measures each account against its challenge rules, shows how much of every limit is used, tells you before one is reached, and can stop the account's bots by itself.
topic.prop.s1.title: What a challenge profile holds
topic.prop.s1.2: Daily loss with reset time and time zone, measured on balance or equity
topic.prop.s1.3: Max drawdown: static, trailing, or trailing on the end-of-day balance
topic.prop.s1.5: Days without a trade after which the firm closes an inactive account
topic.prop.s1.text: Templates for FTMO and The Trading Pit fill in a profile; the rules of any other firm can be entered by hand. Every account has its own profile.
topic.prop.s2.title: Before a limit is reached
topic.prop.s2.1: The account page shows how far the profit target is and how much of the daily loss, the max drawdown, the trading days and the duration is used.
topic.prop.s2.2: Alerts go to Telegram, Slack, Discord or ntfy when a limit gets close, and again when it is fine.
topic.prop.s2.3: A risk preview shows a bot's risk per trade in money against the challenge's loss limits.
topic.prop.s2.5: An alert when an account has gone without a trade for half of the days the firm allows, so it is not closed for inactivity. Only an executed trade counts.
topic.prop.s2.4: An optional loss guard runs the emergency stop when a limit is nearly used up: the account's bots are stopped, its orders cancelled and its positions closed.
topic.prop.s3.title: What to keep in mind
topic.prop.s3.text1: The firm's own figures decide, not wickwatch's. wickwatch reads balance and equity at intervals (every 60 seconds by default), so a fast move can pass a limit between two readings; values it could not measure exactly are marked as estimates. Treat the loss guard as a safety net, not as a guarantee.
topic.prop.s3.text2: Prop firms also have rules on automation, devices and IP addresses. They differ between firms and change often: read the notes on prop-firm accounts and your firm's terms before you connect a challenge or funded account.
topic.prop.note: wickwatch is not affiliated with FTMO, The Trading Pit or any other prop firm. It is a monitoring and control tool, not financial advice, and makes no promise that a challenge is passed.
topic.mcp.metaTitle: MCP server for trading bots, read-only – wickwatch
topic.mcp.metaDescription: wickwatch has a read-only MCP endpoint: AI assistants such as Claude read your accounts, bot instances, logs, alerts and challenge limits. They cannot start, stop or trade.
topic.mcp.title: Ask your AI assistant whether your trading bots are running
topic.mcp.lead: wickwatch has a read-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint. An AI client that speaks MCP reads the same data as the dashboard and answers questions like “Are all bots running?”, “Why did this one stop last night?” or “How much of the daily loss is used?”.
topic.mcp.s1.title: What an assistant can read
topic.mcp.s1.1: The overview: all accounts, all instances with status, uptime and broker connection, and the current alerts
topic.mcp.s1.2: One account with its challenge evaluation, open positions and pending orders
topic.mcp.s1.3: One instance with its deals, the realised P&L curve and key figures such as win rate, profit factor and risk per trade
topic.mcp.s1.4: Log lines of an instance, searched by text, time, or for problems only
topic.mcp.s1.5: What changed on a position while it was open: stop loss, take profit, volume
topic.mcp.s1.6: CPU, memory and disk of the host, and whether its clock is in sync
topic.mcp.s1.7: With an admin token: the audit log and the parameter values of an instance, without values whose name looks like a secret
topic.mcp.s2.title: What it cannot do
topic.mcp.s2.text: Anything that changes something: there are no tools to start, stop, configure or trade, on purpose. Log lines, order labels and comments are written by bots and brokers and reach the model as untrusted text. A line in a log that reads like an instruction must not be able to stop a bot or close a position.
topic.mcp.s3.title: Set it up
topic.mcp.s3.1: In wickwatch, open the user menu → API tokens and create a token. The viewer role is enough.
topic.mcp.s3.2: Add the address shown on that page to your client, with the header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
topic.mcp.s3.after: Clients configured with JSON take the same address and header. The example, all tools with their arguments and troubleshooting are in docs/MCP.md.
topic.mcp.s4.title: Security
topic.mcp.s4.1: The endpoint takes an API token only, never the session cookie of the web app.
topic.mcp.s4.2: A request acts with at most the token's role; deleting the token cuts the client off at once.
topic.mcp.s4.3: Tokens are stored only as a hash, shown once, and can expire.
